column1: Applied after Tab 1. Up to 3 emotions selected per check-in; use the HIGHEST intensity among them. Intensity 0-10 or Mild/Moderate/High/Very High mapped: Mild=0-3, Moderate=4-6, High=7-8, Very High=9-10. Output is one or more of the EIGHT support pathways: Regulate, Dump, Express, Connect, Execute, Adapt, Reflect, Meditate (Rituals / Prayer) — never a NUCRIPCE driver. v3: rows highlighted in pale yellow are new experience families added in September 2026. Rows marked SENSATION-LED are triggered by a sensation captured at S09 (Body pain; Interoception signals), not by an emotion. v3.2: rows shaded pale lilac are new or changed for Reflect and Meditate.

column4: Intervention triggered
column5: Rationale

column2: Overwhelmed, panicked, can't cope
column4: Regulate (forced primary); Support pathway also surfaced
column5: Matches v2 spec worked example: Low Energy + Very Bad Mood + overwhelmed 6 + no demand -> Regulate + optional Dump.

column2: “too much in my head”, can't organise, can't name it
column4: Dump (primary); Regulate as alternative
column5: Directly matches the Dump intervention's functional question in the v2 spec: 'I have too much in my head and cannot organise or name it.'

column2: Anxious, worried, afraid
column4: Regulate first; if a demand/deadline exists, queue Execute or Express to follow once Regulate completes
column5: Matches founder's own scenario (Section 9 worked example).

column2: Anxious, worried, afraid
column4: No forced intervention — proceed to Demand/NUCRIPCE if a demand exists; offer Regulate as an available alternative
column5: Lower intensity does not necessarily block engagement.

column2: Frustrated, angry, irritated
column4: If Need involves communication: Express (draft without sending) + optional Regulate before completion
column5: Matches v2 architecture's caution against reactive sending.

column2: “I know what I mean but can't get it into words”
column4: Express (primary)
column5: Directly matches the Express intervention's functional question in the v2 spec.

column2: Lonely, isolated, wanting company
column4: Connect (primary)
column5: Directly matches the Connect intervention's functional question.

column2: Sad, down, flat
column4: Regulate and Connect surfaced as co-primary options
column5: Sadness does not always block capacity the way panic/overwhelm does; connection may help.

column2: Restless, can't sit still
column4: Add Regulate (movement-based tools specifically) to alternatives
column5: Restlessness responds well to movement-based regulation specifically.

column2: “This way of doing it isn't working”, frustration with format/environment rather than the task itself
column4: Adapt (primary)
column5: Directly matches the Adapt intervention's functional question: 'the current way of doing this is creating unnecessary friction.'

column2: Excited, joyful
column4: No forced intervention; if Sensitivity flags (Tab 3) are also present, still surface Adapt (environment) before a focus-demanding Execute
column5: Matches source spec's excited+sensory-overload worked example — good mood does not cancel sensory demand.

column2: Calm, content
column4: No intervention required — proceed directly to Demand/NUCRIPCE if present, or Home if support-only and resolved v3.2: Reflect or Meditate available on request (never pushed).
column5: Baseline positive state.

column2: “I've let everyone down”, 'I always mess this up', after a missed deadline
column4: Regulate (self-compassion reset) at High+ -> Express (a short, factual repair message; never auto-sends) -> Execute the smallest repair step. No blame or streak language anywhere.
column5: v3 addition. Shame drives avoidance; the repair step must be tiny and the tone non-judgemental (51.2% of survey respondents quit tools over guilt-inducing notifications).

column2: “I can't move or speak”, blank, numb, going non-verbal
column4: Regulate (forced), tap-only and non-verbal: no typing or speaking required. Connect only as a one-tap pre-written message. Demand deferred. Lowers the band one step (Tab 10).
column5: v3 addition. Reflects the polyvagal 'shutdown' state and the founder's own experience; text-entry flows fail users in this state.

column2: “I want to, but I can't get going”
column4: Execute (primary): 2-minute start on the smallest visible step + body double. Light Regulate first only if the band is Constrained or lower.
column5: v3 addition. 48.4% of survey respondents struggle to start tasks; this is not the same as overwhelm and needs a start, not a reset.

column2: “Everything is too loud”, ears ringing, can't filter
column4: Adapt (reduce input now: quieter spot, headphones, exit plan) + Regulate (Step out, Breathe, Ground) before anything else. Demand deferred unless T0. Lowers the band one step.
column5: v3 addition. 66.0% report sensory overwhelm disrupting daily functioning.

column2: “Just one more thing”, skipped meals, hours gone
column4: Adapt (pace: set a stop point) + Recovery micro-break for body basics -> resume if the user chooses. Reminder, never a lock-out.
column5: v3 addition. A positive state that still depletes capacity later.

column2: Bored, drifting, flat, can't engage
column4: If a demand exists: Adapt (add stimulation) or movement Regulate -> Execute with a Novelty or Interest hook. No demand: nothing manufactured.
column5: v3 addition. Common for ADHD; forcing focus fails.

column2: Drained after people, 'peopled out'
column4: Regulate (Recovery: quiet, low input) primary. Connect NOT offered. Demand capped to Routine or deferred. v3.2: Meditate (silent stillness) offered as an alternative; Reflect only after a re-check shows Blue.
column5: v3 addition. 66.8% of respondents spend significant energy masking; 65.6% find social interaction exhausting.

column2: “Too many things, don't know what matters”
column4: Dump (list everything) -> Execute (prioritise: show 3, user picks ONE). Everything else parked, not lost.
column5: v3 addition. Survey free-text asked for a single 'what matters now' view.

column2: Grieving, bereaved, loss of a role or relationship
column4: Connect and Regulate co-primary. Adapt offered (lighter load, time off). Demand deferred or reduced to the minimum. v3.2: Meditate (remembrance ritual or prayer from the user's own saved practices) offered as a user-chosen alternative; Reflect deferred while grief is High+.
column5: v3 addition.

column2: Pain, migraine, chronic-illness flare, post-exertional fatigue - captured at S09 as a Body sensation with its own intensity
column4: Regulate (Recovery / rest) + Adapt (pace and scope; suggest asking for an adjustment). Demand reduced to the essential or deferred.
column5: Pain is a SENSATION, not an emotion. It is listed here only because it triggers an intervention route. Energy can be low for physical reasons; recommendations must never read as 'try harder'.

column2: Stung by criticism, replaying a comment
column4: Dump (stop the replay) or Express (draft a response WITHOUT sending). Regulate first at High+. No forced positivity.
column5: v3 addition.

column2: Hunger, thirst, needing the toilet, sleepiness or tiredness, feeling too hot or cold - captured at S09 under the sixth sensation category, Interoception
column4: Recovery first (meet the need) -> re-check -> continue.
column5: Interoception (sensing the body's internal signals) is a sensation category, not an emotion. Differences in interoception mean these needs are often missed, so the check-in asks about them directly.

column2: Hopelessness, not wanting to be here, thoughts of self-harm (selected option or free-text flag)
column4: SAFETY OVERRIDE (Tab 7 pattern 28): all layers paused; immediate support screen with fixed, clinically reviewed copy. Never an Intervention alone.
column5: v3 addition. The v2 SOS row only covers SUSTAINED low states over 1-2 weeks; immediate risk needs its own route. Copy and thresholds to be signed off by the Clinical Safety Director.

column2: Can't name the feeling (alexithymia), mixed or changing
column4: Body-first guided check-in (pictures, not feeling words) -> suggest a likely state for the user to confirm. If still unsure: treat as Conditional; never silently assume better or worse.
column5: v3 addition. Many users cannot label emotions reliably; the check-in must still work for them.

column1: Wanting to make sense of an experience
column2: “Why did that go the way it did?”; mixed feelings after a meeting, exam, appointment or disagreement
column4: Reflect (primary): 3 guided prompts, time-limited. At High or Very High (7-10): Regulate or Dump first; Reflect is offered later, only in Green or Blue.
column5: v3.2. Reflect makes meaning after the event. At high intensity, going over an event tends to become rumination rather than reflection (Tab 6c RF-1, RF-2).

column2: “I did it”, “glad that's over”, finished a hard task or event
column4: No forced intervention. Reflect offered (note what helped). If energy is Very Low or Low: Recovery rest first, Reflect saved for later.
column5: v3.2. Capturing what worked builds the user's own evidence for future recommendations and for self-advocacy.

column2: Same emotion family, context or avoided task logged 3+ times in 14 days
column4: Reflect (pattern review, shown in plain words as the user's own data) in Green, Yellow or Blue only. Output can hand off to Adapt (change the setting) or Express (adjustment request).
column5: v3.2. Pattern is presented as self-reported data, never an interpretation or diagnosis. User can switch off pattern prompts.

column2: Worry before an interview, exam, appointment, journey or difficult conversation
column4: Meditate (settling practice, 3-10 min; eyes-open, headphone variant in public) -> Adapt or Execute preparation if a demand exists. At High+ (7-10): Regulate first (Breathe, Ground); Meditate only as an alternative.
column5: v3.2. A calm-enough anticipatory state suits a settling practice; high arousal needs short, body-first regulation first.

column2: “I just need to be still”; “my mind needs quiet, not a task”
column4: Meditate (stillness: silent timer, bell or gentle guidance; length chosen by the user). Regulate Breathe offered as the shorter alternative.
column5: v3.2. Stillness is restful in itself; it is not a productivity step and creates no task.

column2: Wanting to pray, recite, keep a prayer time or personal ritual; feeling disconnected from faith or meaning
column4: Meditate -> Rituals / Prayer using ONLY the user's own saved practice. Adapt if the setting does not allow it (find a quiet or prayer room; silent variant). Connect (faith or community group) optional. At High+ distress: Regulate primary, saved practice shown as the first alternative; Support pathway visible in Red.
column5: v3.2. Faith and ritual are important coping resources for many users. The engine never chooses religious content and never infers faith from profile data (Tab 6c MD-3).

column2: Calm, content; wants to notice what is good
column4: Meditate (gratitude practice) or Reflect (note one good thing) — user's choice. Nothing forced.
column5: v3.2. Positive states do not need fixing; savouring them is optional.

column2: Turning the same thought over for hours or days; “I can't stop going over it”
column4: Reflect BLOCKED (pattern 40). Dump (get it out) or Regulate primary; Connect offered. Meditate only as short, eyes-open, breath-anchored practice. Any risk language -> Safety screen.
column5: v3.2. Stops Reflect from feeding rumination. Different from Rejection sensitivity (row 27), which is triggered by one event.
